name: Image Tool
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
appView.description: Browse every image you generated, with the model, quality and size it was made with.
systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths, up to 16 of them, for editing or compositing several references); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area. COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.5-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the gallery (left sidebar App View, or the tool panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. On older Finch builds, gallery edits arrive as image annotations containing the marked preview and complete request. Hosts with editable-text support instead attach the marked preview (red freehand strokes, numbered pins) as a plain image, with message text listing each comment, its percentage position and the ORIGINAL file path. Use the original path from the annotation or message text. Pass that original path in reference_image_paths, treat the attached marked image as the thing to change, and follow every comment without reproducing the red markup or numbered pins in the result. When the user instead writes their own request, follow that text and treat the attached image as the source. From the sidebar App View — which has no input box — the same edit arrives as a chat message with two images: the first is the ORIGINAL to edit and the second is the marked preview. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to open the Image Tool entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in. That settings menu also holds the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com. The Image Tool button in the Composer toolbar sets the everyday generation defaults instead: default model, default quality and default size (a single image_gen_create call can still override model/quality/size, or base_url for a one-off endpoint). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.
tool.title: Generate Image
tool.description:
Generate an image with OpenAI's GPT Image API, or edit/remix one using reference images and an optional mask.
- Text-to-image: pass only "prompt".
- Image-to-image (reference-guided generation/editing): also pass "reference_image_paths" with local absolute image file paths (several are allowed, up to 16, for editing or compositing references); add "mask_path" to restrict the edit to a masked area.
- size takes "auto" or WIDTHxHEIGHT: 1024x1024 (square), 1536x1024 (landscape), 1024x1536 (portrait), 2048x2048, 2048x1152, 2560x1440, 3840x2160. Custom sizes need multiples of 16, an aspect ratio within 3:1, edges ≤3840px.
- quality: low (fast drafts) → medium → high → xhigh → max. Unless the user asks for better, stay on the cheap defaults (flare + low + 1024x1024); higher quality and larger sizes cost more and take longer.
- background "transparent" (with output_format png/webp) gives a cut-out image; output_format png/jpeg/webp plus output_compression control the file.
- For a slow single render, partial_images 1-3 streams low-resolution previews so progress stays visible.
Generated images are saved to local files and collected in the gallery (left sidebar App View, or the tool panel in a session), where the user can preview images, draw lines and add multiple numbered comments. Gallery edits arrive as image annotations on older Finch, or as a plain marked preview plus editable message text on capable hosts. Both carry every comment, its position and the ORIGINAL file path: pass the original path in reference_image_paths, follow all comments, and never reproduce the annotation marks in the output. Use wechat_send or Session attach afterward to show/share the images — do not try to re-download or re-encode them yourself.
Requests go to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in this mini tool's settings menu in Toolcase (default api.openai.com); pass base_url to override it for a single call only.
A failed call returns the API error code plus a remediation hint — change the prompt, size or inputs as instructed rather than retrying unchanged.
dialog.apiKey.desc: Paste your OpenAI API key. It is stored locally and only sent to the API endpoint used by Image Tool — never shown in chat.
dialog.baseUrl.desc: OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. a proxy/relay endpoint. Leave empty to use the official {default}.
dialog.invalidUrl.title: Invalid URL
dialog.invalidUrl.message: "{value}" is not a valid http(s) URL. The base URL was not changed.
result.fromPartial: The endpoint streamed previews but no final image, so the last preview was saved — it may be lower resolution than requested.
error.noKey: OpenAI API key is not configured. Ask the user to open the Image Tool entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu → "OpenAI API Key" to enter it, then retry.
error.tooManyReferences: Too many reference images: the API accepts at most {max} per request.
